newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary sees further dynamic foreign trade rise.
newsitem.headline: Hungary sees further dynamic foreign trade rise.

text.p: Hungary's foreign trade figures for May show the growth rate of both exports and imports will be between 10 and 13 percent this year, the industry and trade ministry said on Wednesday.
Deputy State Secretary Lajos Berenyi told a news conference foreign trade expansion was likely to continue and that the country was likely to meet its $3 billion trade-deficit target.
"I do not have any reason to change our earlier economic forecasts," he said.

According to customs statistics data released on Wednesday, the accumulated trade gap widened to $1.04 billion in May from $910 million in April, with $659 million of the trade deficit contributing to the current account's gap.

Imports increased by 13.8 percent year-on-year in the January-May period in dollar terms, while exports rose 13.8 percent, with the differential between them narrowing to 0.3 percent from 1.7 percent in the first four months of the year.
But imports are likely to rise by one or two percentage point more this year than exports, the ministry said in a statement.
Berenyi said gross domestic product (GDP) would rise by 2.5 to 3 percent in 1997, while industrial output would increase by 5 to 6 percent and investments by 10 percent.
"We expect GDP growth to exceed substantially the statistical office's 1.2 percent quarter-one figure," he said.

Berenyi said the pace of 7.2 percent year-on-year rise in real wages in the January-April period was likely to slow down later this year and the rise would increase the volume of retail trade and household savings and private consumption, without jeopardising meeting the trade gap target.
Consumer goods imports are likely to rise by 5 to 6 percent this year, he added.
The inflow of foreign direct investment was $556 million in the first four months of the year and was likely to reach levels between $1.8 billion to $2 billion in 1997, he said.
He added the 1996 machinery industry investments of foreign companies such as IBM, TDK, Sony, Bosch, contributed substantially to the rise in exports.
Machinery industry accounted for 87.5 percent of the total export increase in the January-May period, the ministry said.
The machinery industry makes up 43 percent of Hungary's exports and 28.6 percent of imports.
Industrial exports would continue to rise dynamically, the ministry said.
"After a 28 percent rise in the first quarter and regarding substantial exports capacities to be introduced, a more than 20 percent industrial exports rise in 1997 cannot be excluded."
